not_found: ESP32-S3 screw-terminal / expansion board: none in Robotistan, Direnc, Motorobit, Robolink, Robo90 or Robot Sepeti. The only ones are for 38-pin classic ESP32 (Motorobit 242.40), and they fit neither the 44-pin S3 N16R8 nor the S3-Zero. Use F-F jumpers on the board's soldered pins plus a mini breadboard instead.

Cheap GC9A01 bare module with header pre-soldered: Robotistan 351.50 has no header (bare holes) and Motorobit's round PCB 545.40 has a loose header. The only solder-free eyes are the Waveshare-type connector-plus-cable modules at 873.92-1515 TL each.
MPU6500 pre-soldered (Motorobit GY-6500 ships with a loose header) and BMI160 pre-soldered (Direnc, loose headers). The only probably-soldered IMU is the Robotistan MPU6050 (photo only).

VL53L0X pre-soldered: Robotistan states it ships unsoldered; Direnc, Motorobit, Robo90 and Robot Sepeti GY/CJMCU versions are out of stock; TOF050C, TOF400C and CJMCU-531 have loose headers. Only the Robolink TOF250 (with cable, qty 4) or a TCRT5000 board avoid solder.
Grove-to-female-Dupont cable (needed to use the Robot Sepeti Grove VL53L0X without cutting wires): not found in stock.
Any PAM8403 module with headers or terminals: all PAM8403 boards are bare pads except the 4-channel XH-A156 with connectors.

Pre-soldered I2S amplifier (MAX98357A): the Adafruit one at Robot Sepeti ships unsoldered and Robo90's is out of stock. No pre-soldered I2S DAC either (Motorobit PCM5102A, header state not verified, qty 6).
INMP441 pre-soldered: Direnc's ships with loose headers; Robo90, Robolink and Motorobit are out of stock. MAX9814 and MAX4466 also come with loose headers.
Ready-made 2S Li-ion (18650/14500) pack with BMS and leads: none. Only 2S LiPo packs (no BMS) and bare cell holders exist.

Solder-free 5 V regulator of 5 A or more that works from 2S: XL4015/XL4016 terminal modules need an 8 V minimum input; SY8205 5A, Pololu D24V50F5 (Robotistan 2247.99) and Direnc XL4015 have bare pads. The largest solder-free 2S option is a 3 A UBEC.

Single cell plus 5 V 3 A boost without solder: every powerbank/boost module found (Motorobit 242.40/333.30, Robolink 141/55.50, Robo90 XL6009 178.56) needs the cell soldered to pads, and 3 A would not cover 9 servos anyway.

Genuine Wago 221 at the six electronics shops: only Motorobit PCT/F-series clones. Genuine Wago appears only on Amazon.com.tr, which could not be opened (HTTP 503), so its price and ship-from-Turkey status are unverified.
Any product page on Amazon.com.tr: all fetches returned HTTP 503.
A header-soldering service sold by any of the six shops (searched 'lehimleme hizmeti'): none.
soldering_help: None of the six shops sells a soldering or assembly service; a search for 'lehimleme hizmeti' found nothing. Armut.com lists hundreds of 'lehim yapımı' providers in Istanbul (469 'Lehimci', rated 4.7, in districts such as Şişli, Kağıthane, Sarıyer and Çekmeköy; some advertise DIP/SMD prototype and hobby work). They quote per job and publish no prices: https://armut.com/istanbul-lehim-yapimi. No Ankara listings turned up. Neighbourhood phone or TV repair shops are the other practical option. I found no published price for soldering a few header strips, so ask for a quote. For scale, the current Tarçın build needs about 2x2 Super Mini strips, 2 GC9A01 rows, plus the IMU, ToF, INMP441 and PAM8403: roughly 80-100 joints, about 20-30 minutes of work. Maker spaces in Istanbul: Atölye İstanbul (Bomontiada, Şişli; paid membership; whether it has soldering stations was not confirmed) and Maker Atölye (Büyükdere İş Merkezi, 4.Levent; focused on kids' education). No Kadıköy FabLab could be confirmed. For children, Deneyap Teknoloji Atölyeleri is free for 36 months and includes an 'Elektronik Programlama ve Nesnelerin İnterneti' track; applications go through deneyap.org, and the 2026 window (Jan-Mar) has closed. Municipal course centres (ESMEK, BELMEK, gençlik merkezleri) run free courses, but I found no specific 2026 soldering class. Sources: armut.com, fablabs.io/labs/makeratolye, deneyap news (gazetebirlik.com, dha.com.tr).
